sourceEvidence: A monic quadratic Q and polynomial P satisfy Q(x)²+Q(x+2)²=xP(x) for all real x. The task asks for R(1), where R is the remainder on dividing P by Q(x+2).
solutionEvidence: At x=0, Q(0)²+Q(2)²=0, so real-valued Q has roots 0 and 2 and monic Q=x(x−2). Then xP=x²(x−2)²+x²(x+2)²=2x⁴+8x², so P=2x³+8x. The divisor Q(x+2)=x²+2x; modulo it x²≡−2x and x³≡4x, hence R(x)=16x and R(1)=16.

sourceEvidence: A monic cubic f satisfies equal remainders upon division by x+1 and x−2, and f(2x−1)+f(x) is divisible by x²−x. Find f.
solutionEvidence: Write f=x³+Ax²+Bx+C. Equal remainders give f(−1)=f(2), so A+B=−3. Divisibility by x(x−1) gives H(1)=2f(1)=0, hence C=2, and H(0)=f(−1)+f(0)=0, giving A−B=−3. Thus A=−3,B=0,C=2 and f=x³−3x²+2.
